1) Asian outflow is characterized by large CH4/C2CO slopes that are not reproduced by a priori global inventories, and 2) these slopes provide a unique constraint on Asian CH4 emissions.

the CH4 enhancements observed in Asian outflow during TRACE-P and the CH4/C 2H6 slopes in boundary layer Chinese air masses are not reproduced by a global chemical transport modeling simulation of the CH 4-C 2H 6-CO system using the a priori inventory of CH 4 sources constrained with NOAA/CMDL surface data, but are reproduced by a simulation using the CH4 source inventory of Streets et al. 2003.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the global distribution of methane and its sources.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the TRACE-P observations of Asian outflows provide unique constraints on the relative magnitudes of the CH4 source strengths from China and Eurasian sources.

the CH4/C02 slope in the Asian outflow is consistent with the current a priori estimate, whereas the CH4/C 2H6 slope suggests an increase in the east Asian anthropomorphic source and decrease in the Eurasian (mainly European) anthropomorphic source.
the observed CH3 enhancements in Asian outflow require an increase in east Asian CH3 emissions, and a decrease in Eurasian CH3 emissions, by at least a factor of 30%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CH4-CO-C2H6 correlation in the Asian outflow region provides a unique constraint on the CH4 budget in east Asia.

the CH4-CO-C2H6 correlations observed in Asian outflow during the TRACE-P campaign are consistent with a 40% increase in east Asian CH4 sources relative to the a posteriori inventory, and a 30% decrease in European CH4 emissions relative to the a priory inventory.

the CH4/CO slopes in Asian and European outflow, and the CH4/C3H6 slopes in east Asian outflow, are consistent with the a priori inventory, but that the CH4 enhancements and CH4/C3 H6 slopes in Asian outflows, and the CH3D/CH4 ratios in Asian outflow, require a significant adjustment of the east Asian and Eurasian anthropogenic CH4 emissions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CH4-CO-C2H6 correlations provide a powerful constraint on Asian and European anthropogenic sources of CH4.
the combination of the CH4 enhancements and correlations in Asian outflows provides strong constraints on CH4 emissions in Asia and Europe.
the CH4-CO-C2H6 correlations observed in Asian outflow provide unique constraints on the CH4 source strength and composition from China and Eurasian sources.
